text:
Olivia: FYI running a spike on customer X's Private deployment — observed a big drop in KV prefix cache hit-rate vs Hosted/Dedicated. numbers below.

Samir: ugh, how big?

Olivia: from our perf job: Hosted hit-rate ~87%, Dedicated ~84%, Private ~62%. p50 token latency for generation went from 12ms -> 28ms on Private for common prefixes. p95 shows much larger tail.

Darren: that's large. any change in kernel selection/batching? or purely cache misses?

Olivia: profiling shows miss storm causing extra kernel cold-starts and smaller batches. kernel selection churn is secondary — most time lost in netstore fetchs and extra Kv cache populate ops.

Maya: do we have examples of keys that miss in Private but hit elsewhere?

Olivia: yes — sampled 5000 recent keys. pattern: Private keys often include ephemeral query params or a different path prefix inserted by the customer's proxy. examples:
```
/ctx/tenant-42/prompt/v1?trace_id=abc123
/ctx/tenant-42/prompt/v1#L=234
/ctx/tenant-42/prompt/v1?session=mobile-7
```
hosted/dedicated had those normalized to `/ctx/tenant-42/prompt/v1` in our ingress normalization layer (we canonicalize query/fragments), but customer's VPC front proxy strips or re-orders things and the netstore layer receives the raw path.

Kai: so it's a key entropy problem, not model tokenization. Can we canonicalize at the runtime edge in Private? VPC constraints sometimes block our control plane patches.

Olivia: that's the tricky bit. Private control plane is customer-managed. We can't push code into their proxy, but we can change the runtime's keying function. Right now keying is: `sha256(service + path + raw_query)` which preserves order. If we switch to canonicalization step before hashing we should fix it.

Darren: patch idea?

Olivia: prototype function I tested locally:
```
function canonical_path(req) {
  let url = parseUrl(req.path);
  let params = Array.from(url.params.entries()).sort();
  return url.pathname + '?' + params.map(kv=>kv.join('=')).join('&');
}
// then hash(service + canonical_path)
```

Maya: looks good. cost of canonicalization per-request? negligible compared to netstore roundtrip.

Samir: but what about ordering in existing cached keys — this will change key namespace and invalidate cache until warmup. That's a rollout risk.

Olivia: agreed. warmup plan I propose: 1) Add a dual-key lookup for 2 deploys: try canonicalized key first, then fall back to legacy key. 2) Backfill the canonical keys via background prefetch of top-N prefixes for each tenant. 3) When canonical key hit-rate stable (>90% for 72h), flip to canonical-only.

Kai: background prefetch in Private has constraints: many customers block outbound egress to our hosted netstore. Their netstore is usually NFS/S3 in their VPC. Prefetch agent would need to run inside their VPC. Can we trigger a local warmup job as part of runtime startup?

Olivia: yes — two options: (A) runtime-start warmup: scan recent requests from local journal and populate canonical keys on startup; (B) scheduled warmup worker that runs inside the cluster fetching top prefixes from a telemetry snapshot. Option A works without cross-VPC egress.

Darren: how large is top-N? can we be conservative?

Olivia: for customer X, top-500 prefixes cover ~68% of requests. top-200 covers ~50%. I recommend start with 200 to limit load. Also use exponential backoff and concurrency cap to avoid thundering herd.

Samir: any change needed to batching heuristics? you mentioned smaller batches when miss storm hits.

Olivia: yes — observed the runtime's continuous-batching window shrinking because miss latency increased per request and scheduler reduced batch windows to keep latency SLOs. Two mitigations: temporarily increase max-batch-delay for Private clusters under high miss-rate and enable opportunistic batch merging when keys map to same model/kernel.

Kai: hooking opportunistic merge needs to be careful with memory pressure on KV caches. We should metric spike.

Maya: infra-bot, can you schedule a canary with dual-key fallback and warmup-startup for customer X's Private env? low-risk flag.

infra-bot: deploy queued: canary=private/customer-x; flags=[kv_dual_lookup,startup_warmup,opportunistic_batch_merge]; estimate 30m rollout to canary hosts. monitor: kv.hit_rate, batch_size_p50, gen_token_latency_p95.

Darren: nice. after canary, we'll collect: hit-rate by key variant (legacy vs canonical), batch size distribution, kernel churn. If that looks good, schedule gradual ramp.

Samir: one more thought — add telemetry to log sanitized raw vs canonical key mapping (sampled) so customers can audit. keep sample rate low 0.1% for privacy.

Olivia: done — added to canary config. I'll follow up with a short runbook for SRE on rollback triggers: kv.hit_rate drop, p95 > 2x baseline, or netstore error 5xx spike.

Maya: thanks Olivia. this gives a clear path.

Olivia: thanks team. will post results in #eng-runtime after canary finishes. :rocket:
